raw_response: {"diagnosis": "Batch 14 was re-delivered at 05:00 on 2026-01-19, so about 340 txn_ids appear twice in raw_transactions. The re-delivered copies store txn_ts as epoch milliseconds (1768716261000 = 2026-01-18 06:04:21 UTC, identical to the original row), which breaks the TIMESTAMP cast and double-counts those transactions in every gold table. The fix is to parse epoch-millis timestamps and keep one row per txn_id, taking the earliest ingest.", "decision": "fix", "confidence": 0.6, "pre_sql": [], "step_overrides": {"silver_transactions": "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS WITH d AS (SELECT * FROM raw_transactions QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY txn_id ORDER BY ingest_ts, batch_id) = 1) SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id, customer_id, CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id, CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount, CASE WHEN regexp_matches(txn_ts, '^[0-9]+$') THEN epoch_ms(CAST(txn_ts AS BIGINT)) ELSE CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) END AS txn_ts, CAST(CASE WHEN regexp_matches(txn_ts, '^[0-9]+$') THEN epoch_ms(CAST(txn_ts AS BIGINT)) ELSE CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) END AS DATE) AS txn_date FROM d WHERE status = 'POSTED';"}}
